feed.title: Convention for tagged hash tags in BIPs

entry.title: Convention for tagged hash tags in BIPs
entry.summary:
In the discussion surrounding Bitcoin Improvement Proposals (BIPs), a notable inconsistency has arisen regarding the labeling of tagged hashes with either a descriptive name or the BIP number itself. Traditionally, some BIPs, such as BIP 458, initially utilized descriptive names like "HalfAgg/randomizer" before receiving official numbers. This practice was also adopted in the drafting phase of BIP 459, labeled "FullAgg/..", which was later changed to include the BIP number in alignment with more recent cryptographic BIP practices.
This shift has sparked a debate on whether changing tags to conform to recent conventions justifies potentially breaking the specification. The necessity for a tag to be defined prior to a BIP being considered ready and numbered has led to inconsistencies across various BIPs. For example, while BIPs 324, 340, 352, 374, and 445 incorporate their respective numbers within their tags, BIPs like 341 ("TapLeaf") do not, despite being authored simultaneously with other numbered BIPs by the same developers.
The argument for including BIP numbers in tags hinges on the unique identification it provides within the ecosystem, simplifying the traceability and origin recognition in codebases and test vectors. Conversely, the counterargument suggests that since specifications may still be under development when numbers are assigned, incorporating them prematurely could necessitate additional modifications across existing implementations. Furthermore, there's a viewpoint suggesting that tags need not be unique across all BIPs, allowing for broader interpretation and application.
The community is yet to reach a consensus on this matter, resulting in ongoing discussions about whether a formal convention should be established or if an official documentation of this tagging practice is necessary. The resolution of this debate could influence future practices in how BIPs are tagged and identified, impacting both the development and implementation phases of Bitcoin protocols.
